method: Slice fux: executives of company A who became named executive officers of company B. Candidates came from (a) the market screen of CEO changes at companies whose pay-versus-performance TSR showed heavy losses, (b) EDGAR full-text searches of 8-K Item 5.02 filings (2016-2026) for appointments describing a prior role as 'Chief Financial Officer of', 'Chief Executive Officer of', 'President of' or 'Chief Operating Officer of' a company whose stock fell, and name searches on departing CEOs, CFOs and other named executives of such companies, and (c) known executive moves. Every fact was then checked in SEC filings only: A's stock test uses A's 10-K Item 5 performance-graph table or a proxy pay-versus-performance table, B's pay uses B's proxy Summary Compensation Table 'Total' column, and tenure and exit dates come from 8-Ks and proxies. A case qualifies when a tabulated window whose base date and end point both fall inside the person's tenure as a named executive officer of A shows a loss of at least 40% ($100 to $60 or less) or a shortfall of at least 50 points against an index or peer group in the same table, A's public float reached about $500 million, and the person became a named executive officer of a US-listed B after the loss window and no later than three years after leaving A. The longest in-tenure window was used (the earliest in-tenure base, then the latest in-tenure point from a table with that base); a case was rejected if a longer or earlier-based in-tenure window in A's own filings failed the test. Intermediate points inside the chosen window are shown in the notes, including any where A was ahead. Cases were rejected when the only in-tenure graphs were image-only or untabulated, when the in-tenure window missed both bars, or when B came more than three years after A. Pay years reported only outside a proxy (for example in 10-K Part III) are mentioned in notes, not recorded. Quotes are verbatim from bt.text.document_text output (whitespace and typographic variants normalized). Exit pay is recorded only where a filing quantifies it.
